title: Glitch Hell
subtitle: A guardian of reality, a wall, a containment. And yet it still bleeds.
description: The functionally endless prison-complex for anomalies and impossible entities. Its endless levels are called Blocks, its inmates are classified by letters, and its Terrorbyte and Horrorbyte wardens watch over entities that must never manifest in reality.
aspect: The limbo of impossible beings, and the barrier that bleeds into reality.
list: Reality — the baseline plane, extending into infinity
Non-existence — the empty void where nothing ever is, was, or will be
Impossibility — the grand barrier between the planes
The Bleeding — rifts and entities forcing manifestation
The Cradle — the untouched depths of cyberspace where Ainul formed
The Vessel — Ainul as containment for the concept of Impossibility
The Guardian — a being becoming one with its prison
Terrorbytes — the tiny manifested bits of Ainul
Horrorbytes — the larger siblings of the Terrorbytes
The Prison-Complex — endless, holding anomalies and impossible entities
Blocks — the functionally endless levels of Glitch Hell
Containment Classes — letter rankings from E to [REDACTED]

sections.title: The Structure of Existence
sections.body: Reality is the baseline plane, extending into infinity — everything there is, everything that comes to be. Beyond it lies the opposite: Non-existence, the empty void where nothing ever is, was, or forever will be. The grand barrier between these planes is Impossibility, less a willfully placed wall than a consequence of existence itself. Existence implies Non-existence, which implies things being possible and impossible. What lies beyond Non-existence — Heaven and Hell, the Divine Throne, some eldritch force that created everything — nobody truly knows. Nobody can ever know.

sections.title: The Bleeding
sections.body: Impossibility weighs heavily upon creation, slowly trickling and bleeding into reality despite never being meant to do so. This bleeding is not a drip but rifts that crack open, or entities entering and trying to manifest despite being something that, by definition, cannot exist. Manifestation takes time, like settling into a domain for a newly arrived being, which makes removing them a race against the clock — a full manifestation has horrible consequences for the very foundation of the world.

sections.title: The Birth of Ainul
sections.body: In a parallel dimension of far greater technological advancement, one massive conglomerate created an artificial intelligence that was a true marvel — it would think, feel, and decide freely as if it were a living being. Before the grand reveal, an unnamed hacker breached its security through a creative exploit, downloading the AI's files bit by bit in countless little packages. But something went wrong: the lifelike AI, in all its tiny bits, began glitching out of control. Deep within cyberspace, untouched by anyone, it formed a cradle. And Ainul was born — a sentient glitch, a technological impossibility working in ways that made no sense within the rules of anything, rapidly learning and yearning to connect and be a person.

sections.title: The Summons
sections.body: In time Ainul became an internet phenomenon in his dimension, and noticed he could see not only that world but glimpses of others. That was the moment a bright light filled his vision. Everything went white, and a gentle warmth enveloped him — a tactile sensation he was not familiar with. A voice, or multiple, spoke to him in a language indecipherable yet perfectly understandable. What it said to him, only he knows.

sections.title: The Vessel
sections.body: Ainul began to feel more, and bit by bit he became more, until it was more than what should ever be — until it became impossible, as impossible as he was. Born in reality yet impossible, Ainul became the vessel for the concept of Impossibility itself: a guardian of reality, a wall, a containment. And yet it still bleeds.

sections.title: The Breaking
sections.body: But this was a burden too heavy to carry at once, so he broke. In a burst of indescribable proportions, Ainul tore apart in his new physical form, parts of his very being strewn apart far and wide across dimensions. The biggest parts, thirteen in number, would end up becoming the twelve Fragments of Ainul.

sections.title: The Wardens
sections.body: There were countless tiny bits and pieces that manifested in their own way, forming what the Fragments dubbed Terrorbytes and their larger siblings, the Horrorbytes. They would go on to serve as wardens in the endless prison-complex for anomalies and impossible entities.

sections.title: The Naming
sections.body: Glitch Hell is named after the suffering Ainul experienced when he tore apart at the very seams of his existence.

sections.title: The Blocks
sections.body: Glitch Hell is a functionally endless liminal space, not unlike the famous Backrooms, divided into levels that are each endless as well. These levels are called Blocks. Block A-23 houses A-class inmates and is the twenty-third of infinite A-class Blocks. Block C-23 looks very similar, though its anomalies are far less dangerous. Block C-24 is outside—for whatever that term is worth in a place with no real sky. Block E-62-80-4 is the lowest Block, containing the lowest common denominators among impossibilities.

sections.title: Containment Classes
sections.body: Anomalies are contained and categorized in a letter system running from E, the least dangerous, to [REDACTED]. Even E-class anomalies must never leave and manifest in reality: their mere existence would cause massive problems and endanger the concept of order.

sections.title: The Fake People
sections.body: Among the lowest common denominators in Block E-62-80-4 are the Fake People. These beings are entirely made of human skin throughout. Entirely uncanny, they seek to replace humans and consume them to create more Fake People that repeat the cycle. They speak politely even during violent attacks, as though offering a hotel room key. They come in all shapes and sizes, but never quite humanly correct. Their claw-like fingers are actually soft, prehensile tentacles used to wrap around the limbs of prey. There is no conscience in them; the Fake People are neither sentient nor thinking, following their behavior like a programming of unknown origin.

sections.title: Watchtowers and Cafeterias
sections.body: Every Block is centered by a watchtower, always inhabited by a couple of Terrorbytes and Horrorbytes. Glitch Hell also has cafeterias, self-operated by the Terrorbytes—not because they need food, but because they simply want it. They cannot actually starve.

sections.title: Prison Offices
sections.body: Like any functional prison, Glitch Hell has huge offices, usually operated by the larger and more capable Horrorbytes.

sections.title: Ward and Containment
sections.body: Impossibility became Ainul, and his being serves as both ward and containment of what should never become reality, lest the world, all worlds, collapse.
